sentences.text: This tiny pterosaur had a wingspan of slightly under 25 centimeters, making it smaller than almost all known pterosaur specimens.
The generic name Nemicolopterus combines Greek words meaning forest, dweller, and wing.
The specific name crypticus comes from the Greek word for hidden.
The type specimen of Nemicolopterus crypticus is cataloged as IVPP V-14377 and is housed in Beijing, China.
The fossil was discovered in western Liaoning Province in northeastern China.
The original describers concluded the specimen was a sub-adult based on bone fusion in the toes, gastralia, and sternum.
A 2014 analysis placed Nemicolopterus in a sister group relationship with Sinopterus gui.
A 2023 revision concluded that Nemicolopterus could not be assigned to Sinopterus or Huaxiadraco and is now considered an indeterminate sinopterine.
Nemicolopterus is classified within the unranked family Tapejaromorpha.
Nemicolopterus lived in the Jehol Biota 120 million years ago.
The fossil was found in the Aptian-age Jiufotang Formation, dating to 120 million years ago.
The time range for Nemicolopterus is estimated between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.

Researchers debate whether Nemicolopterus was a distinct species or a hatchling of Sinopterus, with some arguing that early bone fusion indicates a juvenile status, a view supported by a 2021 study that formally identified it as a young juvenile or hatchling of the genus Sinopterus.
